about: Vectors for mpp/charge/usdc/stacks. R_S is the usdc draft's A.3 request (draft-usdc-charge-00, blob ec7fc1868b) without description, externalId, feePayer and feePayerAddress. The transaction is built at test time with @stacks/transactions 7.6.0 from these inputs, signed by the private key whose scalar is 1 (compressed); its length, bytes and txid were computed with stacks.js txid(), noble sha512_256, Python hashlib and OpenSSL, which agreed. The fixture transaction L's argument hexes are those of that transaction (Clarity serialization: uint, the sender and recipient standard principals, (some H)); block 9021832 at tenure 256356 is a Stacks mainnet block. The reference's nonce is a decimal string (references are JSON). Integers in L are decimal strings, read as bigints. M4's wireHex is that transaction's bytes, whose SHA-512/256 is the txid, for buyer-side tests without the SDK. A credential's transaction is read as a Stacks node (stacks-core 4.0.5) decodes it; agreedRefusals gives the refusals that reading answers. The status read takes the origin's confirmed nonce before the transaction, so nonce-used is answered only from a nonce already at or above the reference's before the lookup found nothing (SIP-005: a transaction is valid only at its origin's next nonce). The confirmed nonce read answers the nonce with the height of the API's chain tip read after it (GET /extended's chain_tip.block_height), so the nonce read is at or below that height, and a transaction read that finds nothing answers notFound, and one that finds it unmined answers its status, each with the height read before it, so an empty or dropped lookup shows the transaction unmined only up to its own height: nonce-used needs it at or above the nonce read's. An unmined row that names no height reads as null, which is never nonce-used. Rows with txAnswer give the transaction read's answer as is: values of none of its documented shapes, which status reads as pending unreadable and recover refuses stacks/unreadable. recover reads a failed transaction's tenure and the tip's as status does: it refuses stacks/not-success where status gives the failure bitcoin finality, the tip's tenure at least 256358, two above block 9021832's, and stacks/not-final below that or where a tenure read rejects.

pattern.proves: The payer signed a Stacks transaction calling a contract's `transfer` with this ATR's hash as its fourth (memo) argument. The chain verified the signature, the transaction executed with status success, and the memo is in the mined transaction on chain. This does not show that the contract is a SIP-010 token, or that amount, payee, asset or timing match the ATR's content.

agreedRefusals.about: Refusal codes the specification leaves to the implementation, as this package applies them. Each row's wireHex is M4's signed transaction with one part replaced, as its case says (its payload, its post-condition, its authorization, or its payload and anchor mode), sent as the credential's transaction (base64, stacks_transaction_v1). Every row is what stacks-core 4.0.5 reads (StacksTransaction::consensus_deserialize): the package answers mpp/stacks-tx-malformed for bytes a Stacks node does not decode and serialize back to the same bytes, and mpp/stacks-memo-not-h for a transaction it decodes that does not call transfer with (some H) as its fourth argument. Row 0's tenure change ends one byte into its last 20-byte field, which a node reads as truncated. Rows 1 to 13: a token transfer's recipient (payload type 0) and a pay-to-alt coinbase's (type 5) are each a principal, and a Nakamoto coinbase's is none or (some <principal>); any other value there is refused, whatever its depth, and stacks-core reads (some …) of another value as no recipient, which it writes back as none. A function argument nests at most 16 levels, the outermost counting 1. Rows 14 to 24 hold a Clarity value in a transfer's fourth argument: a tuple has members, named by Clarity names of up to 128 characters and written in name order as bytes; a list's items have a least common type; a string-ascii holds alphanumeric, punctuation and whitespace bytes only, and a string-utf8 well-formed UTF-8, a byte-order mark included; a value's type is at most 1,048,576 bytes (MAX_VALUE_SIZE), a list's type its length times its item type's size plus a few bytes, and (some …) its value's type plus 1; a contract principal's name is a contract name of up to 128 characters. Rows 25 to 30: a smart contract names a Clarity version from 1 to 7, and its code is printable ASCII, tab and newline; a contract call's contract name has 1 to 40 characters, its function name is a Clarity name and its address version is below 32; a coinbase is anchored on chain only. Rows 31 to 34: a Nakamoto coinbase's VRF proof parses, its Gamma the canonical encoding of an Edwards25519 point not of small order and its s a scalar below the group order. Row 35: a poisoned-microblock payload holds two headers that differ and share a sequence number or a parent. Rows 36 to 38: a post-condition's contract name has 1 to 40 characters, its asset name is a Clarity name, and its address version is below 32. Rows 39 to 41: a multisig authorization holds exactly the signatures it requires, an order-independent one at least that many. Rows 8 to 12 carry the coinbase bytes and VRF proof of stacks-core's own Nakamoto coinbase test, and rows 31 to 34 that proof with one part replaced: its Gamma in rows 31, 32 and 34, its s in row 33. Rows 42 to 45 are M4's transfer built and signed again with @stacks/transactions 7.6.0 from M4's inputs, its version and chain id set to the row's transactionVersion and chainId before signing; every byte but those and the signature is M4's. A Stacks node takes a transaction only for its own chain id, and only at its network's version: 0x00 on mainnet, 0x80 on any other network (stacks-core 4.0.5, stackslib/src/chainstate/stacks/db/transactions/processing/validation.rs L49-79), and a mainnet node's chain id is 1 (stackslib/src/config/mod.rs L1844-1857; chain ids 1, 2147483648 and 2147483649 are stacks-common's CHAIN_ID_MAINNET, CHAIN_ID_TESTNET and CHAIN_ID_SIGNET, stacks-common/src/libcommon.rs L58-61). M4's challenge names chainId 2147483648, so the package answers stacks/chain-mismatch for each: bound, reference and build's complete alike. Rows 46 to 48 hold the size bound, which bound, reference and build's complete share: a transaction is 1 to 16,384 bytes, and an empty one or one over 16,384 bytes is mpp/stacks-tx-malformed, the code of bytes a Stacks node does not decode. Row 48 is M4's transfer with a fifth argument, a buffer of zero bytes, built and signed with @stacks/transactions 7.6.0; with a buffer of 16,053 bytes it is 16,384 bytes, which the three take, bound reading H from its fourth argument.

buyer.about: The buyer gate's rows for this file's pairings, in the form of buyer.json's rows. B2 is the plant: the document advertises H, the hash of the ATR in B6's first check, and the link serves the planted ATR, that ATR with one byte changed; the gate declines hash-mismatch and never calls the signer. B6 is the pairing's bound check over the payment this file already holds: check(ATR, presented) gives H, and check(planted ATR, presented) declines signed-not-bound. Where the ATR is abc, H is its SHA-256 (FIPS 180-2 B.1) and the planted ATR is abd. SHA-256 values are GNU coreutils sha256sum, which openssl dgst -sha256 matches. Bytes are hex. A B2 input names the account, the buyer's inputs and the time (now, in seconds) its build needs. noSignedPayment names each pairing of the file that has no B6 row, and why.

boundChallenge.case: The file's credential at `credential`, a JSON Pointer (RFC 6901) into this file, presented with its echoed challenge replaced by `challenge`, the same challenge with the change the row's case names: pairingsOf, over the challenge as issued, does not name `pairing` for it, and that pairing's bound and reference refuse the credential with the row's code, the code pairingsOf gives (mpp/not-this-pairing where it names other pairings). The request is base64url, without padding, of its RFC 8785 form, except where the case says otherwise.
